notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts cash contributions from PACs, unions and businesses to county commissioner, sheriff, clerk, assessor and treasurer candidates, reported to the Oklahoma Ethics Commission since 2023 (none were found). Oklahoma bans corporate contributions to candidates, so most outside money comes through PACs. Individuals, candidates' own money, tribes, in-kind gifts and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Oklahoma yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Rogers County Sheriff's Office operates two drones as of 2017, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Residents also pay Rogers County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Debt service leaves out $895,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the city did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: no candidates for mayor and council of City of Catoosa were matched to contributions reported to the Ethics Commission since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 9 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Catoosa's borders in OpenStreetMap (8 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Oklahoma yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 8 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Catoosa's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is recorded for some; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
